data.hypothesis: The catalog contains five distinct valid tile programs; the 16-row, 32x4 variant measured 2.816 µs and the selected 16-row, 32x8 parent measured 3.223 µs, while other shapes were slower in their recorded samples. Keep the 16-row tile and test a contrasting 32x16 CTA: one output per thread may reduce serial work, but the 512-thread block could raise resource or scheduling costs. No benefit is assumed.
data.notes: This changes the selected 16-row tile's Y launch width from 8 to 16 threads. A strided cooperative-load loop initializes all 24 shared rows, including halos; the boundary mapping leaves q=63 unchanged and wraps only q<0 or q>63. The stencil expression, full output writes, A input, and unused B/scratch behavior are preserved. No local correctness or timing run was performed; controller validation should include signed varying inputs and independent endpoint values before repeated official timing. Recorded parent samples vary substantially, so compare measured runs without attributing a cause from averages alone.
transformations: Retain a 16-row Y output tile and 32 contiguous X lanes, but increase the Y thread dimension from 8 to 16 so each thread computes one output row.
Use a ceiling-count cooperative load loop with a bounds guard so all 24 shared rows, including both four-row halos, are initialized with this launch shape.
Preserve the stencil expression, complete output coverage, input and scratch behavior, and explicit period-63 boundary mapping.
